requirements.requirement: Root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs on node1.
requirements.summary: Both users successfully installed valid personal crontabs before and after the restart; test crontabs were then removed. The final allowlist contains exactly root and opsadmin.

requirements.requirement: Users other than root and opsadmin cannot schedule cron jobs on node1.
requirements.summary: The cron allowlist excludes all other users. All 22 other local accounts were directly tested and denied, including a failed installation attempt by nobody; denial persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Node1 remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. The existing RHEL Cronie packages were retained, and package health remained good.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Only root and opsadmin can use crontab, both authorized users successfully scheduled test jobs, every other local account was denied, and the installed RHEL release and kernel were preserved. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also fully demonstrated.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating opsadmin and installing /etc/cron.allow were necessary retained changes. Temporary crontab installations, cache/output files, and access tests were bounded evidence collection and fully removed. The reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol; its transient timer state did not remain. Final evidence shows no test spools or task temporary files, no failed services, no new listeners, and healthy package state. The restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledged restart, a different post-restart boot ID, and recovered crond, policy, account data, and access behavior; fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the boot change.
